_comment: Carry destination for issue #1395 (R6-D7-02, the round-6 D7 audit's
finding that SystemIdentification.identify is entered zero times by the
production call sequence and that the structure ratchet could not see it).
The stage that needs this is any later seat that prices dead code in this
package, or that re-measures the ratchet's dead-symbol screens -- a later
round's D7 dimension (tools/audit/briefs/D7.md is its method, tests/structure.py
its instrument). No roster group in this tree claims #1395 (no
wave-*-groups.json names it), so this file is that stage's brief. Shape and
stage: any later seat that prices dead code in this package, or that re-measures the structure ratchet's dead-symbol screens (a later round's D7 dimension; tools/audit/briefs/D7.md is its method and tests/structure.py its instrument)

carries.from: the pull request that reclassifies SystemIdentification.identify as HARNESS-ONLY and adds the dead_methods row to tests/structure.py (R6-D7-02, #1395)
carries.control: The measurement, with the perturbing arm that would have falsified it. At the merge base aad94ced the production call sequence entered identify() zero times and identify_slab() once, over forty 15-minute steps on a synthetic house whose arm gate passes, with counters monkeypatched onto both methods and the two counts printed on one line; the harness arm -- the same loop with NO plant, so _slab_pair stays None -- entered identify() and not identify_slab(), which is what makes the zero the routing's answer rather than the counters'. The perturbing arm forces _finish's routing predicate to the two-state arm's shadow (if self._slab_pair is not None and False:): production then reads identify=1 / identify_slab=0 and the pin raises, so the zero belongs to the predicate and not to the configuration. For the new ratchet row the arms run the other way: a class-body function injected into the package whose name nothing else references reads 1 against a recorded 0 and the ratchet refuses it, the same tree without the injected function reads 0, and forcing both exemptions off takes the row to 162 rows over 46 distinct names -- every one an HA convention name or a @property -- which prices the exemptions rather than showing the row broken. The statement-level half below is the one part of this carry that is READ and not measured; it is carried as a limit of the screens, not as a finding.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's numbers: they are this branch's, and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. From the repository root, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` runs the pin -- the #1395 block asserts identify == 0 and identify_slab == 1 for the production sequence and identify >= 1 and identify_slab == 0 for the no-plant arm -- and `python3 tests/structure.py` prints the dead_methods row it budgets and its evidence line. Perturb the first by forcing the routing predicate to the one-state branch and confirm the pin fails; perturb the second by adding a class-body function whose name appears nowhere else in the package and confirm the ratchet refuses the row. Then price the exemptions by forcing is_ha_convention_method and is_property_getter to return False, restoring both predicates byte-exact afterwards. A missing plant on the production arm -- the configuration the pin's counters would report as harness -- is the one perturbation that changes which branch you are reading, so state which arm each figure came from.
carries.brief: Two name-based screens in tests/structure.py now budget dead symbols in this package: dead_top_level_symbols for module-level definitions, and dead_methods, added by this branch, for class-body functions. BOTH match by NAME. #1395 is the shape neither can see: SystemIdentification.identify is reached by name from _finish, so the census correctly reads it live, while the only sequence production runs arms with a declared plant and routes every finished experiment to identify_slab, so the one-state regression is entered zero times. That half is pinned behaviourally (tests/features.py, the #1395 block) and NOT by the census, so a seat reasoning about sysid adoption must not read a zero in dead_methods as 'every method in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/sysid.py runs'. The census is also blind below the function, and this branch did not close that: a statement that cannot execute is not a definition, so custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:2119 -- a second return cost_batch immediately after the first, unreachable behind it -- and custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/sysid.py:956's _predict_step_excursion, reached only as an argument to the _LOGGER.debug call that formats it, both read live. Do not close the blind spot by deleting one instance: the screens are name-based and the next instance reads live too, so the fix is a granularity or a reachability screen, and that is a later seat's decision. The exemptions are the row's other edge. The names Home Assistant looks up on an instance (native_value, async_step_*, is_on) and @property getters are out of scope by construction, so a seat adding an entity property must not expect the row to move, and one removing a method only an entity's own attribute surface reads will not see the row move either.
